description.value: The study investigated whether risk-taking bias in adolescents is associated with functional reward anticipation and gray matter density in the ventral striatum before possible substance abuse.

spans.text: In this study, we investigated whether risk-taking bias in adolescents is associated with decreased striatal reward processing and therefore shares the neural correlate of addiction prior to a possible onset of substance abuse.

value: we suspect that the link between risk-taking behavior and drug addiction may stem from a common neural basis: a relative hypoactivation of the ventral striatum prior to initial substance abuse.

description.value: The Cambridge Gamble Task assessed risk-taking bias. Participants guessed which color contained a hidden target and then chose points to bet; risk-taking bias was the average percentage of points bet when the more likely option had been chosen. It was used to characterize risk-taking behavior.

spans.text: The measure of risk-taking bias was the average percentage of points bet given that the participant had chosen the more likely option.
